{{Field procedure|summary=Diagnose cargo, bin, and incoming-fragment blockages and restore refinery processing without venting useful progress unnecessarily.}}

Use this procedure when a ship's [[Refinery]] stops accepting useful fragments, a completed bin does not transfer a tonne into cargo, or collectors continue working while refinery progress has stalled.

A refinery bin holds progress for one commodity. At 100%, it creates one tonne and transfers that tonne into a [[Cargo Rack|cargo rack]]. A full cargo hold leaves the completed bin occupied until enough cargo space becomes available.<ref name="refinery">[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Refinery Refinery], Elite Dangerous Wiki. Accessed 15 September 2026.</ref>

== Before you start ==

* Stop extracting new fragments until the blockage is identified.
* Hold the ship in a safe position away from rotating asteroid surfaces.
* Let any fragment already beneath the cargo hatch finish delivering, then inspect the right-hand inventory and refinery information.
* Decide which commodities are worth preserving before using '''Vent'''. Venting a bin discards all progress currently stored in that bin.

== Diagnose the blockage ==

Check these conditions in order:

# '''Cargo capacity:''' look for at least one free tonne of cargo space. Limpets and existing commodities count against the same capacity.
# '''Completed bins:''' a bin at 100% with no free cargo space is waiting to transfer a tonne.
# '''Occupied bins:''' if every bin contains a different partial commodity, a newly delivered resource without a matching bin cannot be assigned.
# '''Incoming resource:''' identify any resource waiting in the incoming processing area because no matching or empty bin exists.
# '''Module state:''' confirm that the refinery is powered, enabled, and functional.

The refinery processes mined commodity components. Raw Engineering materials use separate material storage and do not fill refinery bins.

== Procedure ==

{{Procedure steps|
# If cargo is full, create at least one tonne of space. In the field, discard or abandon only cargo or excess limpets that the run can safely lose; at a station, sell or transfer cargo instead.
# Watch the refinery after space becomes available. A completed bin should transfer one tonne into cargo and become available for further processing.<ref name="refinery" />
# If cargo space was not the problem, compare the occupied bins with the commodity the run is trying to keep.
# Select the least valuable unwanted partial bin and choose '''Vent''' only after confirming its name and percentage. The stored progress is permanently lost.
# If the incoming processing area contains an unwanted resource, discard that resource rather than sacrificing a useful high-progress bin when the interface offers that choice.
# If every occupied bin is valuable, stop collection and preserve the partial progress. Return to unload cargo or accept that the current refinery cannot process another commodity simultaneously.
# Prevent the blockage from recurring by adding unwanted collectables to the ignore list through [[How to Ignore Unwanted Mining Commodities]].
# Resume collection with one useful fragment and verify that its component enters a matching or empty bin, or that a completed tonne moves into cargo.
}}

A blocked incoming area and a full cargo hold are different failures. Venting a partial bin does not create cargo capacity, and discarding cargo does not create a refinery bin when every bin remains occupied by a different commodity.<ref name="hopper">[https://forums.frontier.co.uk/threads/hopper-is-empty-what-is-the-hopper.473341/ Hopper is empty... What is the Hopper?], Frontier Forums community discussion. Accessed 15 September 2026.</ref>

== Completion check ==

The refinery is clear when:

* useful incoming components can enter matching or empty bins;
* completed bins can transfer whole tonnes into cargo;
* no unwanted incoming resource is holding processing open; and
* collector deliveries no longer recreate the same blockage.

Resume normal mining only after one useful fragment completes that path successfully.

== Common problems ==

* '''A completed bin remains at 100%:''' free a full tonne of cargo capacity and confirm that the refinery is powered. Jettisoning less than one tonne of capacity is not possible; remove at least one cargo canister or limpet.
* '''Every bin contains useful partial progress:''' do not vent blindly. Stop collecting that new commodity, preserve the bins, and unload or refit before continuing a mixed-resource run.
* '''The same unwanted bin returns immediately:''' collectors are still bringing that resource. Add it to the ignore list before resuming.
* '''Collectors deliver fragments but no percentage changes:''' look for a blocked incoming resource, a disabled refinery, or fragments whose useful output is a raw Engineering material rather than a refinery commodity.
* '''Cargo was jettisoned but comes back aboard:''' an autonomous collector may retrieve it again. Mark the canister ignored, abandon it where appropriate, pause collectors, or move away before resuming.
* '''The refinery has too few bins for the run:''' a higher-class or higher-rated refinery can hold more simultaneous partial commodities; module selection belongs on the [[Refinery]] reference page.
